title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Stepped Monthly Rates on Demand Service Arrears
content:
| The most recent invoice to fall due | The open position | The monthly rate for each month or part month |
|---|---|---|
| has stood past its due day longer than the tier's suspension period | above the tier's credit limit | 2.0 percent |
| has stood past its due day longer than the tier's payment term | at or below the tier's credit limit | 1.75 percent |
| any other case | any | no stepped rate applies |

The open position read for the second column is what the program invoiced in the fee's window less what
was received in it. The days past its due day are counted from the due day carried on the most recent
invoice to fall due on the rate program.

**The three program figures the rows turn on** under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Suspension period (calendar days past due) | Payment term (calendar days) | Credit limit (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 45 | 30 | 7500 |
| Priority Response Program | 45 | 30 | 15000 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 45 | 30 | 25000 |
| Emergency Response Program | 30 | 30 | 40000 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 30 | 45 | 75000 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 30 | 45 | 150000 |

**Both sides of the figures (hypothetical).** On the Block Hour Service Program, whose suspension period
is 45 calendar days, whose payment term is 30 calendar days and whose credit limit is 25000 US dollars:
an invoice 46 days past its due day on an open position of 26000 US dollars carries the 2.0 percent
rate; the same invoice on an open position of 25000 US dollars carries 1.75 percent, that position
standing at the limit rather than above it and the invoice standing more than 30 days past due. An
invoice 30 days past its due day carries neither stepped rate, 30 days being no longer than the payment
term of 30 days.
